alsoPublished.reason: The page names the rule group it documents: 'VendorName: AWS, Name: AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet, WCU: 50'. The reader was asked for the rules inside the group and listed those; the group's own name is inventory of the group itself.

The page states the same exclusion as the ATP page: 'This rule group isn't available for use with Amazon Cognito user pools.' The reader treated it as prose about the UnsupportedCognitoIDP rule; it is also a stated resource-type exclusion.

coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region count, no Region availability table, and no partition. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing as an enumerated axis. Other AWS services appear only as scope qualifiers - Amazon Cognito user pools as an exclusion, Amazon CloudFront distributions as the only place two rules are evaluated, Amazon CloudWatch as where label metrics land. That is 0 services covered, not 2 or 3. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing enumerated. 'Protection pack (web ACL)' and 'CloudFront distribution' are mentioned as the protected-resource context, but the page publishes no resource-type list and no per-resource-type support matrix. The only dimension this page actually supplies is the catalogue of 16 named rules inside one managed rule group.

features.featureName: Account creation fraud prevention rules listing (rules in AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet)
features.reasoning: The page's only enumerated universe is the set of named rules inside one managed rule group, and the table row is exactly the unit AWS makes a statement about (name, action, labels). The published vocabulary's 'managedRuleGroup' is the wrong grain here - this page IS one rule group, it does not enumerate rule groups - so I use the new camelCase name 'managedRule'. It is catalogue, not external: the rule names exist only because AWS WAF publishes them. Nearest existing vocabulary fit would be 'control', but an ACFP rule is a detection rule with a default action, not a compliance control, so I did not force it. [Axis renamed from the coined name 'managedRule' to the registry's 'managedRuleGroupRule', which denotes the same list. 'managedRule' was left free because AWS Config uses it for something else entirely.]
features.scope: Rule-group scope, plus three stated per-rule conditions. Whole rule group: not available with Amazon Cognito user pools, and it requires configured registration and account creation paths, so all rules but UnsupportedCognitoIDP and AllRequests require a request token. Per rule: VolumetricIPSuccessfulResponse and VolumetricSessionSuccessfulResponse are evaluated only in protection packs (web ACLs) that protect Amazon CloudFront distributions and never inspect HTTP/3 (QUIC) responses; SignalClientHumanInteractivityAbsentLow only inspects the account creation path and only runs if the application integration SDKs are implemented. No Region, no partition, no per-plan dimension anywhere on the page.
features.statuses: 16 rows, all present/included; 0 stated as not supported; 16+0=16. Read as presence only - a row exists iff AWS ships that rule in this rule group. Rule names in table order: UnsupportedCognitoIDP, AllRequests, RiskScoreHigh, SignalCredentialCompromised, SignalClientHumanInteractivityAbsentLow, AutomatedBrowser, BrowserInconsistency, VolumetricIpHigh, VolumetricSessionHigh, AttributeUsernameTraversalHigh, VolumetricPhoneNumberHigh, VolumetricAddressHigh, VolumetricAddressLow, VolumetricIPSuccessfulResponse, VolumetricSessionSuccessfulResponse, VolumetricSessionTokenReuseIp. Secondary attribute stated per row, the default rule action: 11 Block (UnsupportedCognitoIDP, RiskScoreHigh, SignalCredentialCompromised, AutomatedBrowser, VolumetricSessionHigh, AttributeUsernameTraversalHigh, VolumetricPhoneNumberHigh, VolumetricAddressHigh, VolumetricIPSuccessfulResponse, VolumetricSessionSuccessfulResponse, VolumetricSessionTokenReuseIp), 4 CAPTCHA (SignalClientHumanInteractivityAbsentLow, BrowserInconsistency, VolumetricIpHigh, VolumetricAddressLow), 1 Challenge (AllRequests); 11+4+1=16. This action split is an attribute of the same 16 rows, not a second axis.

pageTitle: AWS WAF Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) rule group
shouldNotExtract: The 'Introducing a new console experience for AWS WAF' banner. The VendorName/Name/WCU line (WCU 50 is a capacity cost, not coverage). The repeated Note block about static versions, the changelog and AWS Support (it appears twice, before and after the considerations section). The 'Considerations for using this rule group' prose - pricing, best practices, intelligent threat mitigation cross-links. The whole 'Labels added by this rule group' section: the client session label, the browser fingerprint label, the 2 token namespace prefixes (awswaf:managed:token:, awswaf:managed:captcha:) and the 3 token status label names (accepted, rejected, absent) with their 4 rejected sub-reasons (not_solved, expired, domain_mismatch, invalid) are a shared token vocabulary reused across every intelligent threat mitigation rule group, and are label mechanics rather than a coverage claim. Also not coverage: the many label strings quoted inside the Description column, the risk-score and volumetric threshold numbers (20 requests per 10 minutes, 65,536 bytes, more than 5 IP addresses, and so on), the Example sentences, and the 'See also' Skills for AI coding assistants boilerplate with its agent-toolkit CLI command.
trap:
The most likely misparse is counting labels instead of rules. The Description column is dense with backticked awswaf:managed:aws:acfp:... strings - a label-hungry parser would harvest 50+ 'items' from a 16-row table. Runners-up: (1) treating this page as one item on a managedRuleGroup axis (expectedCount 1) instead of a 16-value rule catalogue, or the reverse - folding these 16 rules into a global rule-group list; (2) reading the shared token-status label list as a second coverage axis and adding 2 prefixes + 3 names + 4 rejected reasons to the count; (3) misreading the Cognito material as per-rule not-supported evidence - UnsupportedCognitoIDP is a rule that IS present, and the user-pool exclusion applies to the entire rule group, so it is 1 stated exclusion at the rule-group level, not 16 No values; (4) splitting VolumetricAddressHigh and VolumetricAddressLow into one 'VolumetricAddress' entry, or collapsing the {{low|medium|high}} template placeholders in the label strings into extra rows; (5) counting rows from the HTML rendering where
tags may split a cell into several visual lines - the table has exactly 16 data rows plus 1 header row plus the --- separator.
whatThePageStates: The page documents a single AWS Managed Rules rule group, AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet (VendorName AWS, WCU 50). It opens with prose about what the rule group does, a considerations section (extra charges, required custom configuration of registration and account creation paths, and an explicit statement that the rule group isn't available for use with Amazon Cognito user pools), then a labels section that describes the shared token-status label vocabulary and the ACFP label namespace prefix. The one enumerated, countable claim is the 'Account creation fraud prevention rules listing' table, which names each rule in the rule group with its description, its default rule action, and the labels it adds. Every row in that table is a rule that the rule group contains; the page never lists a rule that is absent or unsupported, so this is a presence catalogue, not a Yes/No matrix.
